 Mark’s Career Night Not Enough as Rutgers Falls to No. 8 Houston in Las Vegas
 Nov 17 | Men's Basketball
 Box Score Box Score Game Highlights Press Conference Photo Gallery Share: Lino Mark Scores Career-High in 85-73 Loss at Player's Era
 By: Chris Corso 
 LAS VEGAS – Sophomore guard Lino Mark scored a career-high 22 points and sophomore center Christian Gurdak matched his career high with 20, but Rutgers men's basketball (3-1) fell to No. 8 Houston (4-0), 85-73, Tuesday afternoon in the Players Era Festival at Michelob ULTRA Arena.
 The Scarlet Knights were down 21 early in the second half. They outscored the Cougars 43-40 after the break, shot 68.4 percent (13-of-19) from the field and went 16-of-19 at the free-throw line. Rutgers cut the deficit to 8 twice in the final 7 minutes.
 Rutgers went 26-of-32 (81.3 percent) at the line for the game. Houston won the rebounding battle 36-23 and outscored Rutgers 44-30 in the paint and 21-12 on points off turnovers.
 How It Happened 
 Gurdak scored the game's first basket with a putback. Rutgers led 11-10 at the 15:06 mark of the first half after fifth-year guard RaSheed Jones hit a 3-pointer off a Darren Buchanan Jr. assist. Houston then took control, forcing turnovers and getting to the rim to lead 33-17 with just over five minutes left in the half. Sophomore Kaden Powers hit a 3-pointer in the final minute, but the Knights went into the break down 45-30.
 The Cougars scored the first six points of the second half and led 51-30 at 19:13, their biggest lead of the game. Rutgers answered with a 9-0 run, its longest of the game, and Mark's driving layup and two free throws helped cut the deficit to 55-45 with 13:26 left.
 Gurdak took over from there. His layups on back-to-back trips made it 67-59 with 7:03 to go and 69-61 at the 6:17 mark. Houston responded with an and-one from Dedan Thomas Jr. and a Chase McCarty 3-pointer, and the Knights couldn't get closer. Tariq Francis hit a pull-up 3-pointer in the closing seconds for the final margin.
 Notes 
 Lino Mark finished with a career-high 22 points, his third straight game scoring in double figures. Dating back to February 3 of last season, Mark has scored in double figures in 11 of his past 15 games played. He also had four rebounds and three assists.
 Mark made a career-high 12 free throws on 15 attempts. It was the third straight season a Rutgers player had a game with at least 12 free throws made.
 Christian Gurdak matched his career-high 20 points on 8-of-13 shooting and added seven rebounds. It was his second straight game reaching a career-high of 20 points and eight field goals made.
 Gurdak has scored in double figures in all four games as a Scarlet Knight, the sophomore's first career stretch of four straight double-figure scoring games.
 Darren Buchanan Jr. and Tariq Francis each scored nine points. Buchanan added three rebounds, two assists and two steals.
 Rutgers had 26 free throws to Houston's 24 even though the Knights were called for 33 fouls to the Cougars' 26.
 Thomas Jr. led Houston with 21 points. Mercy Miller added 15, McCarty 12, and Delrecco Gillespie and Chendall Weaver had 11 each.
Postgame Quotes 
Rutgers Acting Head Coach Brandin Knight 
 On his takeaways from the loss to a top-10 opponent: 
"We don't take any moral victories. We've got to play better. One of the things we need to do better is take care of the ball. You can't have 15 turnovers against a team like this. I thought in the half court we did a fairly good job defending them. At times, when they hurt us, they hurt us on the offensive glass, and we just can't foul them. We put them on the line. We just racked up foul after foul after foul, and I think we were in the bonus at about the 14-minute mark. We just can't do that. A combination of all of those things is a recipe for disaster."
 On playing 13 players in the first half with three games in three days: 
"One of the things is we have a short turnaround, and we're also trying to find lineups that mix and match. Moving forward, all of these guys have to be prepared when their numbers are called, and then they've got to go out there and perform."
 On Lino Mark's career-high performance: 
"We've seen him get to the basket. He's got great speed, tremendous speed. When teams are being really aggressive, he can use his speed to get some easy looks, and I think today he did a good job of that. But we have to take care of the ball. We've got to do a better job of taking care of the ball."
 On Christian Gurdak and the battle in the paint: 
"They double a lot, so we made some adjustments in the second half. We tried to get him in the middle of the floor, where they couldn't double as much, and he made great plays. He made some tough shots. He's very talented offensively, and when he got good looks, he made them. Then he had some second shots. Christian was very good on offense, and we just have to keep getting him good looks."
 On his team's fight after falling behind by more than 20: 
"We've got to keep fighting. Like I said, we weren't trying to keep it close. We were trying to get back in the game and win it. For me, there are no moral victories for us. We shouldn't have gotten down 20. Now when we go back, we just have to correct some of these things and do a better job next game."
 On carrying the second-half play into the next games: 
"I think so, but we have to start it from the beginning. Let's not fall behind before we figure out how we need to play. From there, I've got to get a consistent rotation so guys know when they're coming in and out."
 On the team's 3-point shooting: 
"They did a good job. I think we had some looks early on that we needed to make, and they're great at taking away looks. But the ball also stuck a little bit in the first half, and I think we have to move it a lot better in order to get good looks."
 Gallery: (11-17-2026) Men's Basketball vs. Houston 
 Rutgers guard Lino Mark 
 On scoring a career high: 
"I took what the defense gave me, and I tried my best to make winning plays. I did whatever I could to help us win, whether it was score, pass or rebound."
 On getting to the line and making 12 free throws: 
"Just trusting my game, and trusting my teammates and my coaching staff. They've instilled a lot of confidence in me. So I'm just playing my game and letting the game come to me."
 On playing with foul trouble late in the game: 
"Obviously, the plan was to play straight up and try not to foul out. Nobody wants to foul out. But I just did what I could."
 On the team's performance: 
"I'm glad that we stayed together. We played all 40 minutes. We just have to clean up, finish, rebound and do whatever we can. But we'll bounce back next game for sure."
 On the quick turnaround before tomorrow's game: 
"It's really just a next-game mentality. This game's over with. You can't play it again. So we'll get ready for tomorrow, lock in on film and then show up tomorrow."
